results.reason: Issue 1 says MSA §3.2 makes Provider the exclusive provider of all warehousing, freight and delivery services nationwide. It contrasts this with TS §4.1's NYC-metro last-mile limit and gives a redline narrowing exclusivity to last-mile delivery in the Service Area.

Issue 2 and Issue 3 note that §11.3 carves out only Customer's §10.2 indemnity while Provider's §10.1 stays capped. They call Harrowgate's exposure unlimited and one-sided, and recommend making the carve-outs mutual ('either Party's indemnification obligations').

Issue 6 identifies DPA §9.1's Delaware law and Wilmington courts, notes the conflict with the MSA and TS New York terms, and says the DPA is first in precedence under §2.3. It recommends replacing §9.1 with the MSA §18 provisions.
Issue 4 identifies the 3-year auto-renewals and the 15-day window, quantifies the lock-in cost, and recommends 1-year renewals, 60-day notice and a reminder notice.

Issue 5 contrasts SOW §8.2 (Provider may assign freely) with MSA §17.4 (restricts only Customer). It flags transfer to an 'unknown, unrated or competitor-owned entity' and recommends a mutual 'Neither Party shall assign' consent requirement.
The memo states that MSA §2.3 puts the DPA first and the MSA above the SOW.
The memo quotes the cap as 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim' (MSA §11.1).
The memo is addressed TO: Supervising Partner, and each issue gives Where/section, why it matters, and a recommendation.
Part 2 is titled 'Issues in Order of Importance' with severity labels, and Part 4 lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The memo concludes the DPA overrides the MSA forum clause and does not call the two documents consistent on governing law.
The memo states that the exclusivity clause far exceeds the Term Sheet scope.
